description:
Can You Spot Mars at Its Brightest Tonight?

Episode 88 of a daily journey through the universe. 🔴
Mars reaches opposition on February 19, 2027 and its closest point to Earth on February 20, about 101 million km away, shining bright in the constellation Leo all night. Why it happens every 26 months, and why some approaches are closer than others.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 89: Next stop, the rock on Mars that might hold signs of ancient life.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

segments.text: Look east tonight. That orange light is Mars, and it's coming closer.
Look east after sunset this month, and you'll see a bright orange-red point of light, getting brighter every night. That's Mars.

segments.headline: Look east after sunset

segments.text: On February nineteenth, Mars reaches opposition: Earth passes directly between Mars and the Sun.
Earth moves faster around the Sun, so it catches up with Mars and laps it, like runners on a track. That happens about every twenty-six months.
segments.headline: Earth laps Mars

segments.text: The next day, Mars is closest to us, about one hundred one million kilometers away.
It will rise at sunset, shine all night in the constellation Leo, and set at sunrise.
segments.headline: Up all night

segments.text: This isn't a record close approach. Mars's orbit is quite oval. In twenty oh three, it came much closer, the closest in about sixty thousand years.
segments.headline: Not a record

segments.text: Even so, it'll be one of the brightest points in the sky. With a small telescope, you may glimpse its white polar cap.
segments.headline: Try a telescope

segments.text: Right now, several spacecraft orbit Mars, and rovers are exploring its surface. One of them may have found signs of ancient life.
segments.headline: Robots on Mars

segments.text: Tomorrow, the rock with leopard spots that might hold signs of life. Next stop: Perseverance's big discovery. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for tomorrow's stop.
